reason: E1 supports the premise that Ti-rich Nb-Ti alloys have better superconducting properties than Nb-Ta alloys, but it does not provide evidence that increasing Ti in a bcc HEA increases the density of states at the Fermi level or that this mechanism governs Tc enhancement. E2 and E3 are irrelevant to these specific mechanistic claims. Thus, the core mechanistic premises lack direct evidentiary support.
premises: Ti-rich Nb-Ti-based alloys (binary, ternary, quaternary) exhibit higher Tc and/or upper critical fields than Nb-Ta-based alloys.
Increasing Ti content in a bcc HEA will increase the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
An increased electronic density of states at the Fermi level strengthens electron-phonon coupling and raises Tc, per BCS theory.
